messages:
maria: quick ping — opened a PR that changes the console metrics schema for tracing hooks, need 1-2 reviews before I can merge into canary branch

sam: looking now, what should I watch for? perf regressions or just schema compatibility?

maria: mostly compatibility. I renamed `trace.latency` -> `trace.request_latency_ms` and added a histogram bucket config. no runtime behavior changes expected, but dashboards need updated queries.

anya: small heads-up: the new name will break the heatmap dashboard if not updated. I can follow up with a patch to the dashboard queries after the merge.

kevin: posting a quick diff comment about the histogram buckets — can we use 0-10/10-50/50-200/200-1000? current buckets look skewed for our p99s.

maria: thanks kevin — updated to your buckets in the latest commit. also added a short migration note in the PR description so ops knows how to backfill old series.

ci-bot: CI passed: unit tests and lint (2m). integration tests queued.

sam: left one minor comment on the schema typedef, otherwise LGTM. I don't have merge perms this week, @kevin can you give it a quick approve so we can get it into the canary window?

kevin: I can approve after integration tests finish. @devops-bot when is the next canary deploy scheduled?

devops-bot: next canary deploy window: 2026-03-20 02:00 UTC. current capacity reserved: 2h. rollback window: 30m.

maria: perfect — if integrations pass I'll request merge 1h before the window. an FYI: dashboard PR is queued and will reference the migration notes.

anya: I'll queue the dashboard update once I see the canary build ID. tagging the metrics-queries owners so they can validate: @sam @anya.

sam: sounds good. if nothing else blocks, I can validate queries after canary is up.

kevin: approve from me pending integration green. thumbs when it finishes. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: integration tests passed (18m). all checks green.

maria: merge requested. tagging release-ops that we'll need a quick rollback plan in case the histogram emits unexpected cardinality: @release-ops

maria: thanks everyone — I'll monitor canary metrics closely once deployed.
